original.title: ⚡ [Performance] Use Promise.all for concurrent reference updates in CMS service

output.title: Run reference updates in parallel with Promise.all in CMS service
output.body:
Reference inserts/removes in `create`, `addReferences`, and `removeReferences` (integrations/cms/service.ts) ran sequentially in a for...of loop, so each independent API call waited on the previous one to finish before starting, wasting time on I/O that could run at once.

Tested: benchmarked sequential vs. parallel with a 50ms mocked API latency across 4 reference groups — sequential ~202ms, parallel ~51ms, ~75% reduction.

original.title: fix: prevent stuck power lock when restarting an offline server (k8s)

output.title: Fix stuck power lock when restarting an offline server (k8s)
output.body:
Restarting or stopping an offline server left the panel stuck on "another power action is currently being processed for this server". A completed Pod isn't auto-removed, so `Terminate` sees it's not running and returns without deleting it, then `waitForPodDeletion` blocks for the full duration (10 min) waiting for a deletion that never happens, holding the power lock the whole time.

- `WaitForStop` (power.go) now checks the Pod first via `getPod`: if it's not found or `!isPodRunning`, it calls the new `markOffline()` and returns immediately instead of falling into the wait-for-deletion loop.
- Extracted the repeated stopping→offline transition into `markOffline()`, reused by both `WaitForStop` and `Terminate`.
- `Start`/`OnBeforeStart` still recreate the Pod on a later start, so no stale-Pod cleanup is lost by skipping deletion here.

Tested: added `TestWaitForStop` (power_test.go) covering both cases — Pod absent, and Pod present but not running; the latter blocks for the full timeout without the fix and returns immediately with it. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./environment/kubernetes/...`, and `go test ./...` all pass.

original.title: security: resolve audit issues — hardcoded passkey, custom MD5, password storage, input validation, typed API, test setup

output.title: Resolve security audit findings: passkey, passwords, validation
output.body:
Fixes 9 findings from a security/quality audit of the frontend and ESP32 firmware: a hardcoded BLE passkey, plaintext password persistence, no input validation on login, and a hand-rolled MD5 implementation.

Behavior changes:
- esp32/niu_led_ble.ino: hardcoded passkey `123456` replaced with `DEFAULT_PASSKEY` (100000), overridable via compiler flag. Only used on first boot; afterwards read from NVS and updatable over BLE characteristic `0xFF07`.
- frontend/src/api.ts: passwords are no longer persisted. `saveCredentials` becomes `saveAccountInfo`, storing only account + country code; `isLoggedIn()` purges the legacy `niu_password`/`niu_cred_version` keys. Old function names are kept as aliases so `LoginPage.tsx`'s import of `getSavedCredentials` still works.
- `login()` now runs `validateLoginInput()` before any network call: account must match `VALID_ACCOUNT_RE` and be ≤100 chars, password ≤128 chars, country code 1–4 digits. Failures throw the new `NiuApiError`.
- The ~90-line hand-rolled MD5 is replaced with the `md5` package (`md5` + `@types/md5` added). `LoginPage.tsx` drops its `savedHash`/`storedHashRef` pre-hash logic since saved account info no longer includes a password.
- `niuGet`, `niuPostForm`, `login`, and `getVehicles` now throw `NiuApiError` carrying the HTTP `statusCode`, instead of a generic `Error`.

What's mechanical:
- New exported interfaces (`Vehicle`, `VehiclePosition`, `OverallTally`, `BatteryInfo`, `BatteryHealth`, `BatteryChart`, `MotorInfo`, `Track`, `TrackDetail`, `FirmwareVersion`, `UpdateInfo`, `LoginResponse`, `LoginToken`) type existing response shapes, each keeping `[key: string]: unknown` for compat with current `Record<string, unknown>` state — most of the added lines in api.ts.
- `react-native-scooter-dashboard/README.md` (36 lines) documents that project as an experimental BLE-only dashboard alongside `frontend/`; no code there changed.

Risk: legacy `niu_password`/`niu_cred_version` keys are deleted, not migrated, so any password cached under the old hashed scheme is discarded on next login check.

Tested: `cd frontend && npm test` — 6 tests passed (`NiuApiError` statusCode/default cases, and 4 `validateLoginInput` cases exercised through `login()`). Confirmed via grep that no `window.location` redirects remain in the API client.

original.title: [autoopt] 20260413-1-trie-changeset-merge

output.title: Merge sorted trie changeset lookups into one cursor walk
output.body:
A samply profile of the trie-input worker showed 98.42% inclusive time in compute_trie_changesets, with 94.94% of samples in InMemoryTrieCursor::seek_exact and 73.30% in cursor_seek. - Added `compute_sorted_changesets` in `changesets.rs`, which does one `cursor.seek` on the first path then advances with `cursor.next()` while the current path is behind, instead of a `seek_exact` per path.
- `compute_account_changesets` and `compute_storage_changesets` now call this shared helper; wiped-storage handling is untouched.

Expected to improve gas_per_second (mgas_s.pct) by >0.3%, per the hypothesis in the session notes; not yet measured against the baseline profile.

output.title: Add block reordering, media preview fixes, and destructive-edit confirm modal
output.body: Editor blocks had no way to rearrange order, and media preview had several reliability bugs: image previews were reported as blocked even when the popup opened, preview navigation went blank on some browsers, audio play buttons stayed active past playback end, and switching tracks quickly could show a stale error. This adds reordering, fixes those preview issues, and adds an in-app confirm step before edits that would drop typed content or attachments. Behavior changes - `EditorDraftSession.reorderBlockByDelta(blockId, delta)` moves a block by -1/+1, renormalizes all `position` values to 0..n-1, and calls `touchDraft()`; `renderBlockList` adds move-up/move-down icon buttons in `.block-item-actions`, disabled at list boundaries. - `openAssetImage` now calls `window.open('', '_blank')` without `noopener`/`noreferrer` before any async work, since those flags made Chrome 88+ return `null` even though the tab opened; it falls back to injecting an `` into the popup when `location.replace(objectUrl)` fails. - `playAssetAudio` tracks playback via `previewAudioPlayback` with `onStart`/`onEnded`/`onError`/`onInterrupted` hooks and a `finalizePreviewAudio(reason)` helper so play buttons reflect active state; a `_previewPlayRequestId` counter makes superseded calls return `{ reason: 'superseded' }` instead of surfacing a stale playback-failed message. - New confirm modal (`showConfirmDialog`, `.confirm-modal*` CSS) gates destructive edits: `getBlockDeletePolicy`, `getOptionDeletePolicy`, and `getSwitchImpact`/`switchQuestionInputTypeWithImpactPolicy` return `confirm_delete` when a block, option, or input-type switch would remove typed text or attached media, `safe_direct_delete` otherwise. - `viewer/main.js` `getInputHelperText('multiple_choice', responseConfig)` now returns "Choose one option only." unless `selectionMode === 'multi'`, replacing the single "Choose one or more options." string used for both modes. What's mechanical `server/editor/main.css` additions for `.block-item-actions`, `.confirm-modal*`, `min-width: 0` on `.block-item-row`, and `flex-shrink: 0` on `.icon-btn` are layout-only, no logic. Tested: full unit test suite (`server/editor/main.unit.test.mjs`, `server/viewer/main.unit.test.mjs`), all passed, including the reorder up/down and out-of-bounds no-op tests, image preview and audio playback lifecycle tests, the audio-switch race test, and the destructive-switch confirm-modal tests. Existing normalization and response-config tests stayed green.

output.title: Rework Honda Nidec control, mutation tests, and CI
output.body:
This branch overhauls Honda Nidec longitudinal control with dedicated PID controllers, replaces the Mull-based safety mutation harness with a Python/tree-sitter runner, and updates CI to match. It also adds a design write-up for persisting the Honda brake PID integrator across power cycles the way openpilot already persists CalibrationParams and LiveTorqueParameters, paired with the opendbc controller-hook PR #545.

What's mechanical
- The Mull/clang-18 mutation harness is replaced by a tree-sitter based Python runner (mutation.py, 633 lines); SConscript probes for gcov via Configure().TryCompile instead of hard-coded LLVM paths.
- setup.sh/test.sh drop the Mull install for stock gcov/llvm-cov, and pyproject.toml adds tree-sitter, tree-sitter-c.
- libsafety_py.py adds load(), mutation_set(), and get_active_mutant() bindings for the new runner; .gitignore drops mull.yml and adds .sconf_temp/.
- routes.py adds ACURA_RDX_3G_MMR and marks five Acura/Honda routes expired or needs-new-route.

Behavior changes (opendbc/car/honda/carcontroller.py)
- gasfactor/windfactor live-learning is replaced by nidec_pid and brake_pid PIDController instances; accel comes from nidec_pid.update() when longControlState is pid, gas isn't pressed and AEB isn't active.
- apply_brake is scaled by brakefactor = 1 + brake_pid_factor and its release is capped to 32 units/frame to match factory behavior.
- hondacan.create_acc_commands drops the gas_force parameter, gating GAS_COMMAND/braking on accel directly; radarless cars get a new IDLESTOP_ALLOW signal after 200 frames (4s) of standstill.
- ACURA_MDX_3G_MMR clips steering torque to ±233/STEER_MAX while braking; ACURA_TLX_1G's STEER_DELTA_UP/DOWN raised to 1.8; ACURA_MDX_3G's torque override LAT_ACCEL_FACTOR moves 1.8 → 3.8, FRICTION 0.19 → 0.11.

original.title: fix: install centaur tool CLI shims in sandbox

output.title: Install sandbox tool shims and gate tool discovery on secrets
output.body:
Live asbx pods run `centaur-agent:main-sha-412d4fc`. api-rs invokes tools-bootstrap's `install-tool-shims --copy-tools`, but the deployed script ignores `--copy-tools`, publishes nothing to `/app/tools`, and `centaur-tools list` comes back empty. This adds the shim installer to the sandbox image and wires it into the entrypoint. The branch also carries an unrelated required-secrets discovery gate and a handful of smaller fixes bundled into the same push.

What's mechanical
- `api/tool_manager.py` has scattered line-wrap and quote-style reformatting (ruff/black) with no behavior change; skim past it.

Behavior changes
- Sandbox entrypoint runs the new `install-tool-shims` whenever `TOOL_DIRS`/`TOOLS_PATH`/`TOOLS_OVERLAY_PATH` is set; `--copy-tools` publishes nested packages into `/app/tools`, skipping (and logging) duplicates by name (`test_install_tool_shims.py`).
- Tool calls now fall back from the tool-server sidecar to the central API on `transport_error`, `404`, or `405`, via the new `tool_request()` in `call.sh` (two new fallback tests in `test_call_sh.py`).
- `ToolManager` skips a tool at discovery if any required secret's env var is unset (`tool_skipped_missing_secrets`); no-op under `onepassword`/`onepassword-connect` (`tool_secret_gate_inactive`). The secret-less sidecar gets an authoritative allowlist via `CENTAUR_AVAILABLE_SECRET_REFS`, and fails open if it's absent.
- The API now mounts `tool_manager.create_rest_router()` directly, instead of relying solely on the dedicated tool-server entrypoint.
- Slack DMs and mpims are always treated as mentions (`is_mention: true`), no text mention required anymore.
- The PostHog CLI gains a `--project-id` flag validated as numeric; the client no longer eagerly resolves `project_id`, since iron-proxy's replace-mode placeholder isn't numeric.
- Codex's `model_reasoning_effort` goes low → high with an explicit `openai_http` model provider; `publish-images.yml` moves the image namespace `paradigmxyz/centaur` → `rwa-xyz/centaur`.

How to review: `services/sandbox/entrypoint.sh` and `install_tool_shims.py` first (the intended fix), then the secret gate in `tool_manager.py`.

Tested: `uv run --with pytest pytest services/sandbox/test_install_tool_shims.py -q`; `uv run --with ruff ruff check services/sandbox/install_tool_shims.py services/sandbox/test_install_tool_shims.py`; `just build-one sandbox`; then `docker run --rm -v "$PWD/tools:/app/tools:ro" -e TOOL_DIRS=/app/tools --entrypoint /entrypoint.sh centaur-agent:latest bash -lc 'centaur-tools list | head; echo count:$(centaur-tools json | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(len(json.load(sys.stdin)))")'` confirmed a non-empty list.
